This should never be done. It is the AnimationTree's role to manage the names of AnimationNodes, and AnimationNodes should not contain names.

As explained in some places like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101564#pullrequestreview-2561174593, an AnimationNode is a resource, so we need to consider the case where multiple AnimationNodes with the same reference are placed in the one blend tree.

I suggest that it should be a generic signal as explained above.

> So, instead of adding a signal called oneshot_finished() to the AnimationTree, we should add a generic abstract signal such as node_notified(animation_node_path, signal_name, signal_variants).

For example, what happens with NodeTransition? Don't we want a signal when BlendSpace is in DC mode and the values switch discretely? What should we use when firing a signal from a custom AnimationNode? I suppose it is not good way to add a new signal to the AnimationTree for them every time.

Also I think it is better to distinguish between signals in StateMachinePlayback and AnimationNode (so signals add to both StateMachinePlayback and AnimationTree) than to mix them up. In case of mix-ups all into AnimationTree, the StateMachine should be named to avoid confusion.

For example, if you follow the description, it must be `MyStateMachine/Outer/Inner/Attack1` not `Outer/Inner/Attack1` since we can't distinguish between two StateMachines that have the same configuration if they are placed same level of the blend tree.

What sort of callable do you imagine, and would it make more sense to use an enum rather than bare strings? Also are there other examples of notification style multipurpose callbacks?

I'll think about it more but from my perspective a lot of these node notify events would be directly caused by user code, such as requesting a transition or changing the blendspace mode, and could be handled by an animation controller script. In comparison, I think `node_started` and `node_finished` would be harder to implement without extra coupling or polling of the tree's state. That said, it probably won't get to the point where the generic signal gets too expensive from unnecessary connections, so the question of which things should be node notified emits or not doesn't really matter. It's also the case that this doesn't need to be decided without some future use case in mind - the state machine signal addresses the proposal use case (and my use case) on its own.

Either way I'll give the generic signal a shot and also break off the state machine changes.

body: Using ENUM is the right direction to go. However, for consistency with something similar to this that already exists in Godot, we recommend the signal name NOTIFICATION_XXX instead of NOTIFY_XXX.

I believe this approach is redundant. At the very least, storing the same String in two places is not the right direction, and we must do indirect mapping, such as storing only the index, and the entity as a String must be only one.

Since the states of internal_active and current_active are not synchronized, it might be better to have an explanation in the documentation that they are “visual” and different from the "internal state".

To give a detailed example, in the case of trying to manage Node state with user scripts, OneShot has been internally terminated already when fading out, so restarting AnimationTree should cause a synchronization discrepancy if you are relying on signals.

It may be possible to add a signal STATE_CHANGED as well as documentation to solve this.

isn't StringName only storing the unified data pointer within either map, so there is just one backing string? this is just to avoid the linear cost of only having `nodes` to determine a name in the current context. ideally there would just be a bimap template available, but alternatively the name could also be copied to `NodeState` at the same time that the base path and parent are set.

I've added `NOTIFICATION_FADEOUT_STARTED` to allow this to be tracked by a user. Currently only one shot nodes emit it since state machines only have crossfade on their internal nodes and that can be fully tracked by the node started/finished events. It also only emits specifically when there is non-zero fadeout, so a bit different from if it was strictly a version of this line but for internal_active.

body:
How about
```
enum AnimationNodeNotification {
  ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_XXX,
  ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_YYY,
}
```
?
Do you think it would be better to parse out the final part of the path or emit the full concatenated path?

The signal must pass the full path to the AnimationNode. As I have said many times, since the AnimationNode is a Resource, the same reference AnimationNodes can be placed in the same hierarchy. To distinguish between them, the user must know the full path.

For example, if you have two BlendTrees with the same reference that have “OneShotA” as a child, you cannot determine which BlendTree's "OneShotA" if the only notification is "OneShotA".
```
BlendTree.tres

[Anim1]
　|
[OneShotA]-[Output]
　|
[Anim2]

---

RootAnimationNode

[BlendTree1(BlendTree.tres)]
　|
[Blend2]-[Output]
　|
[BlendTree2(BlendTree.tres)]
```
In the case above, we should distinguish between `BlendTree1/OneShotA` and `BlendTree2/OneShotA`.

Ah yes that makes sense. I was only considering blend trees as roots but of course the names alone would break if they were nested.

Edit: Although outside of this use case, it still might be worthwhile to split the current map into `StringName -> Ref<AnimationNode>` and `AnimationNode * -> AnimationNodeBlendTree::Node` so that `blend_input` can lookup connections in constant time. I won't do that in this pr though.

Edit 2: Also maybe worth mentioning that although it's not a necessary part of the example, `get_node_name` unfortunately will not be reliable in either case with the tree you've described as both names map to a valid value and it'll return whichever it finds first.

```suggestion
	ADD_SIGNAL(MethodInfo(SceneStringName(animation_node_notification), PropertyInfo(Variant::STRING_NAME, "animation_node_path"), PropertyInfo(Variant::INT, "what")));
```
"node" should be avoided because it is confusing with Node/Node2D/Node3D classes.
Yeah I was thinking about this. The meaning of some of the notifications are frustratingly similar but I agree it's probably best to separate them for clarity and ease of documentation.

Revisiting this, I think actually each of the oneshot, state machine, and transition nodes could use `STARTED`, `FINISHED`, and `FINISHED_INTERNAL` with near identical semantics. At least for next version of this pr I'm planning on having those three constants defined on AnimationNode but use int for the signal/helper method so that AnimationNode subclasses can still define their own notification values and document them individually.

I do have a question as this version of the pr has `FADEOUT_STARTED` as opposed to `FINISHED_INTERNAL` and I've kept the code to only emit that value when there is nonzero crossfade; would you want `FINISHED_INTERNAL` to fire in cases where there is no fadeout?

I am beginning to think that FINISHED_INTERNAL is a little too difficult for users who do not touch the core, so FADEOUT_STARTED might be fine.

> I do have a question as this version of the pr has FADEOUT_STARTED as opposed to FINISHED_INTERNAL and I've kept the code to only emit that value when there is nonzero crossfade; would you want FINISHED_INTERNAL to fire in cases where there is no fadeout?

If there is no crossfade, it is better not to fire. However, if the implementation is too difficult, it is fine to fire it, but perhaps you should note that it fires even if there is no fade-out in the documentation.

Ok, I had to have this on the backburner for a bit but I've updated the pr with per-class enums. I ended up using unnamed enums with manually-made-unique values to be more similar to notification but that can easily be changed to whatever.

I think my only issue with the current implementation is how verbose qualifying the enum is but maybe either the name could be changed or it could be bound as a new globalscope constant. I also noticed a while ago that a state machine with no valid path to the end node never actually finishes (existing behavior; a one shot triggering such a sm will not finish) and included that in the documentation although I'm not sure if it's really the desired behavior?

Edit: Whoops forgot to test with dev flags, the state machine gets started multiple times and one call causes an error due to null process state. In grouped mode it also causes the grouped sm to emit start twice. I'll update with a fix at some point.

I mean at that point would it be best to just have the full enum defined on the base `AnimationNode`? The per signal documentation wouldn't be on the specific node that emits it but at least it would all be in one place and the values would be unique. I think it would be very likely for the user to make the mistake of comparing against a normal string, and it feels weird passing the parameter as a type when it's already a part of how the enum is defined (currently twice).

ed: like if I'm understanding the suggestion, the safe way to check for if any state machine node was finishing for example would be like
```swift
if node_type == &"AnimationNodeStateMachine" and what == AnimationNodeStateMachine.ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_STATE_MACHINE_FINISHED:
```
which was sort of already awkward before but maybe it should just be
```swift
if what == AnimationNode.ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_STATE_MACHINE_FINISHED:
```

```gdscript
if node_type == &"AnimationNodeStateMachine" and what == AnimationNodeStateMachine.ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_STATE_MACHINE_FINISHED:
```
Yes, this is recommended with:
```cpp
ADD_SIGNAL(MethodInfo(SceneStringName(animation_node_notification), PropertyInfo(Variant::STRING_NAME, "animation_node_path"), PropertyInfo(Variant::STRING_NAME, "animation_node_class_name"), PropertyInfo(Variant::INT, "what")));
```
This way may be a bit redundant, but it is the safest way to add a signal to a specific AnimationNode and to assume that the user is specifying the signal by integer number (although converting GDScript's integer to c++ enum should not be done as much as possible). In other words, we need to prevent the addition of signals from breaking the continuity of the sequential numbering, and also prevent the enum constants from changing too often.

Were there issues/regrets with the notification guidance of `You can make your own, but don't use the same numbers as other notifications in other nodes`? I don't think having two parameters here makes it per se safer when the enum values are allowed to overlap compared to if the enum values were not allowed to overlap to begin with. While there is some overhead to checking existing values (ie search the codebase for `ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_[A-Z_]+ = \d+`) I don't think it's too out of question for how infrequently it would happen in this case.

I can definitely just give each class a range of 100 or 1000 values to make it easier though. If that "assigned" range ever ran out adding new values without changing old ones would still possible since values don't need to be contiguous, but probably it would be worth figuring out something different entirely for handling whatever would cause that.

First, I think we can agree on the following two points.

- Signals should be defined for each AnimationNode class
- The number should not be a sequential number across classes

Therefore, overlapping numbers per class, e.g., `ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_ONESHOT_STARTED = 0` and `ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_STATE_MACHINE_STARTED = 0`,  is not a problem.

However, if `animation_node_notification()` only returns int and pathname, there is a problem with users cannot distinguish between them. So in order to solve that problem, animation_node_notification must return the class_name.

I agree with the first point but not the second. I think having repeat notification values and relying on an extra path to be passed is error prone compared to making the enum values distinct across classes, although at least with the current 8 values "started" and "finished" would always be 0 and 1 so if someone tab completed the wrong one of those it would still work (as long as it was also qualified by the type or path). That's why I was asking if more generally there was a consensus about how notifications are split across classes being bad, since that's the closest inspiration for how the signal is defined and used at the moment. It took me only a few seconds to find all the unique `NOTIFICATION_` definitions so I don't think it's too unreasonable for animation notifications to have distinct values.

Edit: also, besides the literal issue of state machines getting started multiple times and the first time being without a context, my biggest issue with this pr is just that the enums are unwieldy - just checking a notification value takes 88 characters and repeats the class twice, but the condition to check that and a type string is 134 and repeats the class three times. I think ideally for me the constants would be distinct, defined per class, and the constant name would omit the class name such that
```gdscript
if what == AnimationNodeStateMachine.ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_FINISHED:
```
would match specifically any state machine node finishing (in 74 characters, for what it's worth lol). Not that character count is the be-all-end-all, but that forcing the type to be specified 3 times to safely check for one particular signal is unnecessary.

The second problem, as raised earlier, is that the sequential numbering is broken when signals are added or deleted. This is unacceptable.

The long enum names are unavoidable in order to conform to Godot's naming rules, and this is not the only area where long enums are used.

> 3 times to safely check 

I don't know what you mean. The type-safe check is only done once by comparing class name StringName, and the enum names and class namespaces just follow Godot's naming rules `AbcXyz` -> `ABC_XYZ_[PARAMATER]`. If you feel it is too long, we can consider to remove the “AnimationNode” prefix like:

```
enum NotificationOneShot {
  NOTIFICATION_ONE_SHOT_STARTED,
  NOTIFICATION_ONE_SHOT_FINISHED,
  NOTIFICATION_ONE_SHOT_FADE_OUT_STARTED
}
```

The reason ONE_SHOT should not be removed here is that it is not possible to determine at a first look which port of the OneShot has started playing if only "Started" is named. `NOTIFICATION_FIRED` or `NOTIFICATION_SHOOTED` may still be okay, but `NOTIFICATION_FADE_OUT_STARTED` is ambiguous again, so I would recommend leaving it.

```suggestion
	ADD_SIGNAL(MethodInfo(SceneStringName(animation_node_notification), PropertyInfo(Variant::STRING_NAME, "animation_node_path"), PropertyInfo(Variant::STRING_NAME, "animation_node_class_name"), PropertyInfo(Variant::INT, "what"), PropertyInfo(Variant::PACKED_INT64_ARRAY, "sub_indices")));
```
Also I suggest adding `sub_indices` so that the transition source and destination can be passed for NodeTransition. If no index is needed (as NodeOneShot), an empty array is passed.

If connect_deferred is used, they may not match when looking at the current Transition state by retrieving the AnimationTree parameters from within the signal. So it is safe to pass them as signal arguments.

Ideally, vararg should be used, but since signals cannot use vararg, so this is a compromise solution.

Also, with this approach, not only NodeTransition, but also NodeBlendSpace2D's DC mode can pass the index of the change destination. I do have a concern though that it needs to be documented what it is.

BTW, in the future StateMachine may be able to have more than one Start State and End State (as I implied in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/88878#issuecomment-1966647736), so this may be useful to notify those indice as well, but it is a tentative plan that has not yet been decided, so don't worry too much about it.

I was thinking about this too, although initially I was leaning towards having an ultra generic `Variant extra` parameter since no obvious subset of state existed between all animation node types. `int[]` probably makes 
sense as the most specific type but I am very uncertain about effectively making adhoc marshaling/encoding a part of the signature and for the semantics to be completely disjoint between node types. It's also a bit of a slippery slope deciding what data gets to be included considering the premise is that the user needs to access a snapshot in time of the state. But then a more general data container would invite a situation similar to [this](https://sampruden.github.io/posts/godot-is-not-the-new-unity/) especially in light of this being a generic signal which is likely being immediately filtered on `what` in the callback.

In c# this question (as well as the enum problem) would be addressed by `EventArgs` but I think the only way to achieve something similar with the godot api would be by creating and passing a `RefCounted` subclass with each emit. This seems to me too expensive to opt all animation tree users into.

Currently I think the best thing would be to have these notifications in places where state is meaningful (ie `TRANSITION_STARTED` having the current and requested states both be populated) and rely on users treating the callback as the correct time to check/process the animation tree state. If there's such a case where the processing absolutely needs to be deferred, an intermediate callback could read the state and pass that to the deferred call.

> The second problem, as raised earlier, is that the sequential numbering is broken when signals are added or deleted. This is unacceptable.

By sequential numbering do you mean specifically having the enum values 0, 1, 2 etc for each class without gaps? In my experience when constants like these are deprecated/removed, a hole is left in the numbering so that serialized data still maps to the correct name. For adding enums, I do think it's best to allocate a large range per class (so its enum values wouldn't have gaps, but also wouldn't start at 0) if mostly for convenience, but even without that I don't think there's any technical problem with having gaps in a given class's notification values (`Node` does this, for example).

> I don't know what you mean. The type-safe check is only done once by comparing class name StringName

I should have been clearer. You're right the `node_type` is the part actually doing the type check in that case but I was talking about literally specifying the type. For example in the following we want to check that a state machine has finished:
```gdscript
if node_type == &"AnimationNodeStateMachine" and what == AnimationNodeStateMachine.ANIMATION_NODE_NOTIFICATION_STATE_MACHINE_FINISHED:
```
The type gets specified in the first equality, the classname itself of course, and then the enum name. Having the name as a separate parameter would be useful if we wanted to define the enum on a common base class or wanted each class to be zero-indexed but I don't think either is correct/necessary here. IMO, it doesn't need to be in the enum name because it always is qualified by the class preceding it, but I don't feel as strongly about this.

I'd prefer to cut out the name there though than to remove `ANIMATION_NODE_` as it might make people think it gets used with `_notification` (also sort of the reason I originally went with a different word entirely, although that too does not scale well in a large codebase). Maybe `AnimationNodeStateMachine.ANIMATION_EVENT_STARTED` would be better if it was acceptable to use a different word than notification.
